# PCA General Assembly Records and Constitution

> Retrieval guide to the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) Minutes, GA1–GA52 (1973–2025), and the BCO and Westminster Standards. The Minutes are page-anchored, OCR-derived Markdown with structured catalogues. RPR catalogue coverage begins at GA18 (1990). GA53 overture research is separate from the completed Minutes corpus.

## Start with the question

Fetch only the sources needed for the question. A wording lookup needs verified constitutional text; interpretation or application also needs relevant Minutes evidence. A historical question needs the wording and numbering in force at the relevant date. The corpus cutoff does not establish the current rule.

- **Current BCO text:** open the [official BCO contents](https://www.pcaac.org/book-of-church-order/) and follow the relevant part/chapter link. Read the provision, qualifications, and cross-references; identify the edition checked. The official current BCO controls present wording.
- **Known BCO provision and its history:** request the provision manifest directly, e.g. [BCO 38-4 records](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/api/bco/38-4.json). For a simple chapter-section reference, the path is `api/bco/<chapter>-<section>.json`. Use the [manifest index](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/api/bco/index.json) for available provisions, suffixes, parent sections, and related entries; follow its `manifest` URLs. Read selected underlying records.
- **Known case, presbytery, overture, or Assembly:** use the corresponding catalogue below and follow its direct source links. An overture number needs its GA/year; a judicial docket year may differ from the year of the Minutes reporting it.
- **Topic without a provision:** search distinctive phrases and synonyms in the relevant catalogues and constitutional text, identify candidate provisions, then follow their manifests. Include STUDIES for doctrinal and denominational-position questions.

## Constitutional text retrieval

- [Constitution Reader guide](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/llms.txt) — routes and data for BCO, WCF, WLC, and WSC.
- [BCO text data](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/content/bco.js) — JavaScript assignments, not a JSON endpoint. `window.BCO` contains chapter objects with `sections` entries identified by `ref` (e.g. `38-4`) and text in `body`; read relevant chapter introductions too. Parse or search as data; no script execution is needed.
- [WCF data](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/content/wcf.js), [WLC data](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/content/wlc.js), [WSC data](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/content/wsc.js) — fetch only the needed book. WCF sections use `ref` and `body`; catechism entries use `n`, `q`, and `a`.
- [Reader and edition notes](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/#about) — check the displayed edition against the official BCO when current wording matters.

The reader is a JavaScript app: a hash URL may return only its shell to a text-fetch tool. Use the content files above in that case. Reader-facing routes include `#bco/38-4`, `#wcf/20.2`, `#wlc/Q.135`, and `#wsc/Q.1`, appended to `https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-constitution-reader/`. These locate constitutional text, not Assembly actions. For current BCO claims, cite the official text actually checked; a reader link can accompany it. Check constitutional status for Directory for Worship provisions rather than treating every paragraph as binding. RAO and OMSJC texts are linked from the official BCO contents; they are separate from the constitutional text.

## Using a provision manifest

Each manifest supplies `provision`, `scope`, `counts`, and `artifacts`. Select by subject and record type using `title`, `matches`, `year`, and `disposition`; retrieve `url` (published page) or `raw_url` (Markdown). `matches` evidence and optional line numbers help locate a passage; `minutes_locators` are leads to verify. `authority_weight` is an editorial sorting aid, not a ruling about binding authority.

Coverage is explicit indexed references in cases, inquiries, CCB overture advice, overtures, and RPR exceptions. It excludes studies and does not infer topical relevance. A chapter manifest does not aggregate its sections, nor does a section necessarily include separately tagged subsections. Use the index to select related entries when the question spans them. A missing manifest, zero matches, or an incidental citation does not establish that no applicable record exists.

## Catalogues by question

- [Judicial cases](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CASES.html) — SJC/CJB docket, parties, disposition, and source records; search case number or party name.
- [Cases by provision](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CASES-BY-PROVISION.html) — BCO, Preliminary Principles, RAO, and Westminster references, with tag evidence. Useful beyond numbered BCO manifests.
- [Constitutional inquiries](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/INQUIRIES.html) — interpretation questions and non-binding advice; verify the answering body and wording in the record, especially for early Assemblies.
- [CCB overture advice](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/CCB-OVERTURE-ADVICE.html) — constitutional review of proposals; pair with the overture's actual Assembly outcome.
- [RPR by presbytery](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR.html) — exceptions of substance and response threads, GA18–GA52. [RPR by provision](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/RPR-BY-PROVISION.html) finds provision-tagged exceptions. Follow each exception's later responses and any SJC escalation.
- [Overtures and outcomes](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/OVERTURES.html) — proposals, answers, and amendment ratification leads. Follow “answered by reference” to the referenced action; verify adoption and any later ratification in the Minutes.
- [Studies and position papers](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/STUDIES.html) — topic-grouped reports, pastoral letters, declarations, and resolutions. Check which recommendations were adopted, received, commended, or recommitted. Some entries have only external PDF sources.
- [Corpus index and volume outlines](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/INDEX.html) — full Minutes and per-volume outlines for floor actions, committee reports, appendices, and records missed by catalogues. Select the actual volume from this list; no GA met in 2020.
- [GA53 overture research](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/index/GA53-OVERTURES.html) — 2026 proposals with prior-action leads; not a substitute for GA53 Minutes or verified final outcomes.

## Expand only where it can affect the answer

Search topic terms as well as provision numbers in the relevant catalogues: records may discuss a rule without citing it. Try spelling, punctuation, party-name, and historical terminology variants. Check material contrary evidence and follow later dispositions, amendments, and cross-referenced actions before concluding.

- [BCO renumberings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raymond-rishty/pca-ga/main/index/bco_renumberings.jsonl) — date-specific predecessor mappings. Read `status` and notes; several mappings are partial or need Minutes verification.
- [BCO changes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raymond-rishty/pca-ga/main/index/bco_changes.jsonl) — amendment-history leads. Verify historical wording and adoption in the underlying Minutes; do not apply a number mapping across all dates.
- [llms-full.txt](https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/llms-full.txt) — optional combined-catalogue fallback when narrower retrieval is insufficient. It contains selected catalogues, not the full Minutes; overtures, RPR-by-provision, and studies still need separate retrieval.

If the catalogues are insufficient, search the relevant full Minutes via the volume outlines. With a local checkout, use `rg` across `index/`, extracted records, and `markdown/`; do not depend on an unpublished database. A truncated fetch is not a complete search: use a raw download and text search, or report the access limit. Stop when the evidence supports the requested scope and material follow-up leads are resolved; an exhaustive historical survey requires broader searching than a wording lookup.

## Verify and cite the evidence

Read the underlying passage before making a material claim. Check the title/case or item identifier, speaker/body, disposition, and context. Separate the court's judgment and reasoning from parties' arguments, dissents, and concurrences; distinguish non-binding CCB advice, RPR findings and responses, committee recommendations, overtures, adopted Assembly actions, and a study report's reception/adoption. A catalogue headnote or provision mention does not establish a holding. Mark your inferences as such.

Use published GitHub Pages `.html` links in answers. Raw Markdown is for retrieval: use a manifest's `raw_url`, or map a corpus path from `https://raymond-rishty.github.io/pca-ga/<path>.html` to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raymond-rishty/pca-ga/main/<path>.md`, dropping the fragment. This conversion applies to corpus Markdown pages, not app routes or JSON assets.

For printed Minutes citations, inspect the `<!-- PAGE ga=… pdf_page=… printed_page=… -->` comment preceding the cited passage in raw Markdown. Rendered text may hide it. For example, `ga=52 pdf_page=885 printed_page=883` yields **M52GA p.883**, not p.885. Copy the source's existing URL anchor; its number need not be the printed page. Extracted records often have no page anchors: use their base `.html` URL. When the record lacks page metadata, follow its source link into the full Minutes. If `printed_page` is null or uncertain, state the available locator and pagination limit rather than inventing a printed citation. Consult the source PDF when OCR, formatting, or pagination affects the claim.

Answer directly with the strongest relevant sources, chronology when needed, and material authority/coverage limits. State the edition and date scope relied on. For a negative result, say “Not found in this corpus,” specifying catalogues, years, provision variants, and topic terms searched. Distinguish an unsuccessful search from an inaccessible source; neither proves that the PCA never addressed the subject.
